notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed. The device is a simulated R0 environment: there is no hardware backend and none was run. The upstream PyBullet environment was never installed, imported or run; PandaEnv.__init__ opens a PyBullet GUI (panda_env.py:26-29), so the fake is the package's own pure-Python kinematic stand-in (F0) and the sim backend (gym.make('panda-reach-v0')) was not run. NOT COVERED: PyBullet rigid-body dynamics, inverse kinematics, contacts, joint limits and rendering; the real render() image is a 720x960 RGB array (panda_env.py:249-273) and is not served by the fake, and the fidelity gaps name the same size. The 24-value observation is returned in full (no reduced array). The fake's end-effector start and object orientation are placeholders; the object start uses the upstream ranges with Python random.Random(seed), which is a fake-only extension because the upstream reset takes no seed (panda_env.py:136,201-205). Five warnings remain: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the seed only records the next reset) and four G8.NO_UNIT: ticks, the reset seed, the seed-class seed and action.values[*]. The first three are the integer inputs the bridge derives and playbook section 8 lists them as expected; action.values[*] is dimensionless because the four action values are normalized [-1, 1] commands scaled by dv = 0.05 (panda_env.py:51-55), so no physical unit applies. There were no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. No operator-required limit and no site-limits overlay: the only physical bound is the environment's own action space (ticks is a structural count bound of the class). Only catalogue classes are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest line the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
